english.title: Fail to comply with police order in relation to a prohibited place
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[failed to comply with the order of a constable not to engage, or to cease to engage, in conduct mentioned in section 4(1)(a) of the National Security Act 2023, namely **(..SPECIFY CONDUCT..), in relation to a prohibited place, namely **(..SPECIFY PROHIBITED PLACE..),]_
(B)_[, having accessed or entered a prohibited place, namely **(..SPECIFY PROHIBITED PLACE..), failed to comply with the order of a constable to leave it immediately]_

(D)_[, being the driver or person in charge of a vehicle or device, namely **(..SPECIFY DEVICE ETC..), in a prohibited place, or in an area adjacent to a prohibited place, namely **(..SPECIFY PROHIBITED PLACE..), failed to comply with the order of a constable to move the vehicle or device from the place or area immediately]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 6(4) and (5) of the National Security Act 2023.

english.notes: Section 6(1) and (2) of the National Security Act 2023 provide officer powers to protect a prohibited place, including ordering a person to cease their activity or move away from the site and arranging for the removal of a vehicle from a prohibited place or area adjacent to it. A constable must reasonably believe the use of these powers to be necessary to protect the safety or interests of the United Kingdom (section 6(3)). This includes the prevention of activity that could harm or disrupt the operations or functioning of a prohibited place in a way that could jeopardise the safety or interests of the UK (see further the notes on section 6.
